chapter: Glen Island, early records and Duke Ellington
title: Existing discographies of Barnet and their inaccurate personnel
summary: He has a couple of discographies, all unreliable on personnel for early dates, and has rarely been consulted.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Is there, to your knowledge, a discography of your recordings?
Is there, to your knowledge, a discography of your recordings, a complete list of everything you did?

Yeah, I've got a couple of them. One that is fairly up to date. It comes -- well, it doesn't have the last record in it. I think it does. It mentions it. '67 and '66. Yes, because it's got a mention of that Reader's Digest date I did, which it says unissued, which is not true. It was issued through Reader's Digest, but not in the stores. But that's actually the last record date. Yeah, this is, oh it's a book, I'd say, about three quarters of an inch thick, and it's got everything listed, and it's pretty thorough. The personnel is all wrong in a lot of things, but -- and then of course Leonard had a discography that was up to a certain year. And then there's another one that comes in two volumes that only goes up as far as '42.
What is the best one that's been done, do you think?

Well, there really isn't any best one. It's -- they all suffer from the same thing, and that is inaccuracy in personnel. They're very good when it comes to, oh, something like, Bluebird, or recent years, you know. But when it gets back there, I guess the records weren't kept very well and they don't know who was on those dates. And of course I have only been consulted about things like that, oh rarely, maybe two or three times. I probably wasn't much help either, you know, because it sort of fades into a was it that date or was it this date. It's very hard to nail it down.
